issue.title: Document --min-confidence in the README CLI options
issue.body:
## Problem

The README examples now show:

```bash
npx context-drift check --changed src/components/user_profile_card.tsx --min-confidence 0.9
```

But the CLI options list documents only `--base`, `--changed`, and `--format`. The new `--min-confidence <number>` option is implemented in `src/cli.ts` but not documented in the options section.

## Impact

Users can see the flag in an example without knowing its valid range, default value, or effect on finding output.

## Suggested Fix

Add `--min-confidence <number>` to the README options list with the valid `0` to `1` range and the default `0.75`.

## Verification

README should make it clear that findings below the configured confidence are hidden from CLI output.

reasons: Exact README flag, range and default identify a checkable documentation change; documentation is allowed by the evaluation profile.

issue.title: Stylistic lint suggestion: `#[must_use]` for types
issue.body:
### What it does

Suggest to mark any type that isn't already marked as  `#[must_use]`, with that attribute.

### Advantage

It is much better/easier to explicitly opt-out of a lint on case-by-case basis
rather than manually keeping track that every type is indeed `#[must_use]`.

### Drawbacks

This would be a `restrict`-type stylistic lint.

### Example

```rust
struct S(u8); // missing #[must_use]
```

issue.title: `help` command is skipped when set `ignore_errors(true)` on the command.
issue.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions/5917
Originally posted by **chungquantin** February 18, 2025 ## Dependencies ```toml clap = { version = "4.5", features = ["derive"] } ``` ## Description Hi, considering the below code: ```diff #[derive(Args)] - #[command(args_conflicts_with_subcommands = true)] + #[command(args_conflicts_with_subcommands = true, ignore_errors = true)] pub struct Cli { #[command(subcommand)] pub command: Command, } #[derive(Subcommand)] pub enum Command { #[clap(alias = "p")] SubCommand(SubCommandA), } ``` By adding the `ignore_errors`, the `help` command of the `SubCommandA` is no longer working. ## How to reproduce an issue? Add `ignore_errors` to any `Command` that contains the `Subcommand` (does have `help`).
CC @chungquantin

comments.author: tmccombs
comments.body:
zsh does support conflicts.

You can see an example of how it is done in the `fd` zsh completions (which are currently manually maintained), such as [here](https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/blob/master/contrib/completion/_fd#L91) where we declare that `--list-details`  conflicts with the `abs-path`, `null-sep`, `max-results`, and  `exec-cmds` groups. 

Basically, when calling `_arguments` you put a list of conflicting options or option groups in parenthesis before the name of the option. 

From [zshcompsys(1)][1]:

> Each of the forms above may be preceded by a list in parentheses of option names and argument numbers.  If the given option is on the command line, the options  and  arguments  indicated  in  parentheses  will not be offered.  For example, ‘(-two -three 1)-one:...' completes the option ‘-one'; if this appears on the command line, the options -two and   -three and the first ordinary argument will not be completed after it.
> ...
> Options can be grouped to simplify exclusion lists. A group is introduced with ‘+' followed by a name for the group in the subsequent word. Whole groups can then be referenced in an exclusion list or a group name can be used to disambiguate between two forms of the same option.

[1]: https://man.archlinux.org/man/zshcompsys.1

issue.title: `missing_asserts_for_indexing` ignores `match` for length
issue.body:
### Summary

lint ignores context of `match slice.len()`

### Lint Name

missing_asserts_for_indexing

### Reproducer

I tried this code:

```rust
// supported: &[u8] is a function parameter, value from enum variant or provided in any other way
// to compile this code u8 can be replaced with anything implementing Display, or Debug (in that case add `:?` to format string)

match supported.len() {
    0 => {}
    1 => println!("{}", supported[0]),
    _ => println!("{} or {}", supported[0], supported[1]),
}
```

I saw this happen:

```
supported[0]
supported[0], supported[1]

 indexing into a slice multiple times without an `assert`
```

I expected to see this happen:
as `usize is not negative and value 0 was explicitly checked, lint should never fire.

### Version

```text
rustc 1.96.0 (ac68faa20 2026-05-25)

commit-hash: ac68faa20c58cbccd01ee7208bf3b6e93a7d7f96
```
